Our convention is that in default configuration we only emit attributes from the semantic conventions. Attributes that don't have semantic conventions should be gated behind a flag e.g. many instrumentations have flags like `otel.instrumentation.grpc.experimental-span-attributes` or `otel.instrumentation.couchbase.emit-experimental-telemetry`.
Another aspect to consider is whether the lite topic name could be presented as part of `messaging.destination.name`. Ideally semantic conventions would provide guidance on this. If you believe that a separate attribute is the best option we can start with this.
you could define your own logger and use that to log the failure

[Javaagent] These common-value scans run even when experimental span attributes are disabled: ordinary receive extraction calls `getDestination()` or `getMessageTag()`, which initializes this entire batch holder. On clients exposing the new getters, this adds two reflective getter calls per message for a homogeneous batch, although neither value will be emitted. Please compute and cache the experimental batch values only when capture is enabled, so the default receive path avoids these extra scans and reflective calls.
Are you sure all of these are needed?
@trask do we have a preference on whether to use `experimental_span_attributes` or `experimental_telemetry`?

replies.body: I think for now `experimental_span_attributes` is most consistent here

threads.body: Does testing all these configurations separately provide value? Perhaps it would be enough to just run one configuration that enables experimental attributes and receive telemetry if that is affected by the experimental flag.

replies.body: I've reduced this to the default configuration and one configuration with both flags enabled. I kept the default run on 5.2 to verify that LiteTopic and priority attributes remain absent when the experimental flag is unset, even when the messages contain those values.

threads.body: Can we switch on `message.getMessageType().name()` and use string constants for the known types, including `LITE` and `PRIORITY`? `toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT)` creates a string for every instrumented send, even on 5.0 with experimental attributes off. Switching on the name lets us handle the newer values without referencing enum constants that are missing on 5.0.

Can we cache handles from `findVirtual` for these getters? All four take no arguments and return `Optional`, so we know the exact signature. `Class.getMethod` can resolve unrelated method signatures while searching. An exact lookup avoids that, and we can still treat `NoSuchMethodException` as an expected result on older clients.
perhaps it would be better to add a case for normal too and change default to `attributes.put(ROCKETMQ_MESSAGE_TYPE, message.getMessageType().name().toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT));`?

[Simplification] Every case in this switch writes the enum name in lowercase: the semconv values are `normal`/`fifo`/`delay`/`transaction`, and the new cases use `lite` and `priority`. The `default` branch already uses that same rule, so one line produces the same values for every type, including ones added later. The `RocketmqMessageTypeIncubatingValues` import would then be unused, so remove it too.

```suggestion
    attributes.put(ROCKETMQ_MESSAGE_TYPE, message.getMessageType().name().toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT));
```

replies.body: The emitted values are equivalent, but the switch intentionally reuses constants for known types to avoid per‑message lowercase conversion and allocation on the send path, including when experimental attributes are disabled. This follows the earlier review feedback: [[https://github.com/open](https://link.wtturl.cn/?target=https%3A%2F%2Fgithub.com%2Fopen&scene=im&aid=582478&lang=zh)](https://link.wtturl.cn/?target=https%3A%2F%2Fgithub.com%2Fopen&scene=im&aid=582478&lang=zh)‑telemetry/opentelemetry‑java‑instrumentation/pull/21276#discussion_r4654382321. The default branch preserves lowercase names for unknown types. I suggest keeping the current implementation.

I pushed a commit to get both. It builds the lowercase names once from `MessageType.values()` into an `EnumMap` when the class loads, so a send is just a map lookup with no allocation. It also picks up whatever types the runtime client has, including `LITE` and `PRIORITY` on 5.2+, without naming them, so it still compiles against 5.0.0. The output is the same as the switch.
